stories.title: Michigan data center map shows 20+ proposals chasing cheap power
stories.dek: A new weekly roundup tracks every active proposal from Monroe to the Upper Peninsula. Residents see the direct link between these projects and higher utility bills plus water strain. The tracker highlights which sites have already secured tax breaks or grid connections.
stories.source_title: Michigan Data Centers: The Weekly Download - Michigan Advance

stories.title: Dozens of data center projects line up across Michigan towns
stories.dek: Crain's maps every active proposal in the state, showing which sites have power deals, tax incentives, or local pushback. Residents 30 miles from any site will see higher electric rates and new transmission lines if these move forward. The list covers metro Detroit suburbs, west Michigan, and mid-state counties.
stories.source_title: Data center proposals have exploded in Michigan. Here’s where all of them stand. - Crain's Detroit

stories.title: Mason County weighs data center impact on local services
stories.dek: Commissioners discussed how proposed data centers could affect EMS, roads and county budgets. Residents in rural Mason County would see higher power loads and possible tax revenue trade-offs. The talks come as more townships face similar project inquiries.
stories.source_title: Mason County Commission discusses community work, EMS and data centers - WV News

stories.title: GenH pitches Morley Dam as hidden data center power source
stories.dek: GenH is floating a plan to use the existing Morley Dam site for a data center that would generate its own electricity. The concept could sidestep some utility fights but still raises questions about water use and local impacts in Mecosta County. Readers nearby should watch how the project is classified under state rules.
stories.source_title: EXPLAINER: Is it a data center? How GenH’s Morley Dam concept would work - Big Rapids Pioneer

stories.title: Township rejects server farm after residents cite noise, traffic, water concerns
stories.dek: Township officials rejected the permit for a proposed data center on Kluver Road. Residents nearby worry about noise, traffic, and higher water use if the project had moved forward. The decision keeps the rural area free of large-scale server farms for now.
stories.source_title: New Buffalo Township board denies permit for Kluver Road site - The Herald Palladium

stories.title: South Haven residents fight rezoning that could open door to data center
stories.dek: Neighbors in South Haven are voicing strong opposition to rezoning the Baseline property, worried about noise, traffic and strain on local services if a data center moves in. The pushback comes as data-center proposals multiply across western Michigan townships. A decision here will set the tone for similar fights in nearby communities.
stories.source_title: South Haven residents oppose rezoning of Baseline property - The Herald Palladium

stories.title: Forsyth residents grill officials on data center power and military ties
stories.dek: Hundreds packed a Forsyth Township hall to question how proposed data centers would affect local electricity rates and water supplies. Officials also fielded concerns about rumored military involvement near the sites. The session gave Upper Peninsula residents their first direct look at the scale of projects eyed for Marquette County.
stories.source_title: Town Hall held in Forsyth Township addresses data centers, military presence - - The Mining Journal

stories.title: Developer sues Gibraltar to overturn year-long data center moratorium
stories.dek: A data center firm claims city officials in Gibraltar illegally blocked its project with a one-year pause. Wayne County residents near the site could see delayed tax revenue and jobs if the suit succeeds. The case tests how far local governments can go to slow large power-hungry facilities.
stories.source_title: Data center developer accuses Gibraltar city officials of unlawfully imposing 1-year moratorium - CBS News

stories.title: Firm behind Mason data center project finally named
stories.dek: A development company has been identified for the proposed data center in Mason. Ingham County residents now know who is behind the project that could affect local power use and taxes. The disclosure gives the community a clearer target for questions about water, noise, and grid impact.
stories.source_title: Development firm behind proposed Mason data center identified - Lansing State Journal

stories.title: St. Joseph County weighs two-year freeze on data center projects
stories.dek: County leaders are debating a moratorium that would block new proposals while they study impacts on roads, water and electricity. Residents nearby worry about higher utility bills and lost farmland. A decision could set the tone for other southwest Michigan townships.
stories.source_title: St. Joseph County leaders debate two-year data center moratorium - WVPE

stories.title: Michigan Officials Face Growing Recall Pressure Over Data Center Decisions
stories.dek: At least 28 officials in eight communities have faced recall efforts tied to data center votes, with only one recall reaching the November ballot, according to a new Bridge Michigan analysis of local fights statewide.

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
